vendor.gs1.title: GS1 barcodes on your parcels
vendor.gs1.lede: With a GS1 company prefix, each parcel gets its own SSCC once it is paid for, printed on its label as a GS1-128 barcode beside our QR: what a receiving warehouse scans into its own system. Without one, your labels carry our code alone.
vendor.gs1.none: No GS1 company prefix: your labels carry our code alone.
vendor.gs1.prefixHint: As GS1 gave it to you: 6 to 12 digits. We never make one up.
vendor.gs1.badPrefix: A GS1 company prefix is 6 to 12 digits.
vendor.gs1.digitHint: One your own systems do not use, so a code is never given twice.
vendor.gs1.claimLede: If prefix {prefix} is yours, send SeeBuyGet staff your GS1 licence for it: the certificate GS1 gave you, photographed or as a screenshot. Those using it are told and send theirs; two members of staff decide whose it is. Until then nothing changes for anybody.
vendor.gs1.licenceHint: A photograph or a screenshot, readable: the prefix and your company’s name on it.
vendor.gs1.licenceReady: Your licence is ready to send.
vendor.gs1.photoFailed: The picture did not go. Try again.
vendor.gs1.d.claimantOpen: You said prefix {prefix} is yours. {names} {n, plural, one {uses} other {use}} it, and {n, plural, one {has} other {have}} until {by} to send {n, plural, one {its} other {their}} GS1 licence; then two members of SeeBuyGet staff decide. Nothing changes meanwhile.
vendor.gs1.d.holderAsk: {claimant} says prefix {prefix}, which you use, is theirs. Send your GS1 licence by {by}: two members of SeeBuyGet staff decide whose it is. Until then nothing changes, and your labels carry on.
vendor.gs1.d.holderSent: Your licence is with SeeBuyGet staff. {claimant} says prefix {prefix} is theirs; two members of staff decide whose it is.
vendor.gs1.d.decidedMine: SeeBuyGet staff decided prefix {prefix} is yours. Their reason: {reason}
vendor.gs1.d.decidedNotClaimant: SeeBuyGet staff decided prefix {prefix} is not yours to print under. Their reason: {reason}
vendor.gs1.d.decidedNotHolder: SeeBuyGet staff decided prefix {prefix} is {claimant}’s: your labels no longer carry it, and the parcels you sent keep the codes they were given. Their reason: {reason}
vendor.gs1.d.withdrawn: The dispute about prefix {prefix} was taken back. Nothing changed.

vendor.price.explainFastest: holds the highest rate any carrier on this route charges, so the first one passing can take it without asking anyone. You are billed that amount now — and once it is delivered, whatever the carrier who actually moved it charges less than that comes back to your balance.
vendor.price.explainCheapest: commits the route to the lowest rate instead. You settle exactly this amount and nothing comes back, but it waits for a carrier at that price.
vendor.price.explainEither: Either way the shops and hubs on the route are paid the fees they publish, and neither price changes after you pick it.
vendor.price.explainAloud: Fastest holds the highest rate so any carrier can take it, and refunds what it did not cost. Cheapest commits the lowest rate and waits for a carrier at that price.
vendor.price.listSub: From the price list: {from} to {to} ({band}), whoever carries it
vendor.price.fastestSub: Any bus can take it — unused ceiling comes back

vendor.store.callbacksNote: Your own website or shop system can hear when your parcels move — paid, ready to collect, collected — and update its orders by itself. Give its web address below. Not needed if you run your store from this app.
vendor.store.cbInfo.title: Messages to your own system
vendor.store.cbInfo.what: A callback URL is the web address of your own system — your website or your shop software — where SeeBuyGet sends a short message each time one of your parcels moves. Your system can then keep the order up to date by itself: mark it paid, email your buyer that it is ready to collect, close it once it is collected.
vendor.store.cbInfo.who: You need one only if your own website or shop system keeps your orders. Running your store from this app alone? Leave it empty: everything is here, and in your bell. Whoever built your website will know what to do with this page.
vendor.store.cbInfo.ev.paid: a parcel’s shipping is paid: its label can be printed.
vendor.store.cbInfo.ev.ready: it is at the buyer’s shop, ready to collect — with its collection code, unless you switch that off below.
vendor.store.cbInfo.ev.disputed: the buyer reported a problem with it.
vendor.store.cbInfo.ev.held: held while its packaging is checked, and released after.
vendor.store.cbInfo.ev.late: running late against the time it was promised.
vendor.store.cbInfo.ev.delayed: expected an hour or more after the time it was promised, its plan made again — said before that time comes.
vendor.store.cbInfo.ev.lost: declared lost after a search — or found again.
vendor.store.cbInfo.ev.hub: a hub took in what you brought it — what came and what did not — or says it did not come.
vendor.store.cbInfo.ev.load: an order sent as freight: a carrier took it, took the goods over, delivered them.
vendor.store.cbInfo.ev.loadDoor: the driver could not hand it over — and, refused at the door, what you decided or the 48 hours did: the load the goods went back on.
vendor.store.cbInfo.ev.loadBack: a driver gave it back before taking the goods over, or it was withdrawn.
vendor.store.cbInfo.ev.balance: money added to your balance, or paid back from it.
vendor.store.cbInfo.ev.test: the test message you send yourself, below.
vendor.store.cbInfo.how1: Each message is sent to your address as a POST with a short JSON body: what happened (event), its details (data) and when (at). Your system answers 200 to say it took it.
vendor.store.cbInfo.how2: Not answered, it is sent again by itself, waiting longer each time, for about two days. Below, each message says whether it arrived; “Send again” sends it once more.
vendor.store.cbInfo.how3: Each one is signed with your store secret: the x-sbg-signature header is an HMAC-SHA256 of the body, which your system checks before it trusts a message. Each carries an id, x-sbg-delivery, the same on every try, so your system can skip one it already took.
vendor.store.cbInfo.test: Try it: give the address, save it, then “Send a test message”.
vendor.store.msg.retrying: Not arrived yet: tried {count, plural, one {once} other {# times}}, tried again by itself {next}.
vendor.store.msg.gaveUp: Not arrived: given up after {count, plural, one {one try} other {# tries}}. Put your system right, then send it again.

vendor.topup.title: Top up your balance
vendor.topup.body: You prepay the shipping; the buyer's share is collected at your checkout and stays your income. Tell us how much you are paying in, and where to send the payment request — your balance changes once the payment comes through.
vendor.topup.waitNote: You said you are paying in {amount}
vendor.topup.waitBody: Nothing has been added yet. When the payment provider confirms it, the amount they confirm goes into your balance.
vendor.topup.checkingBody: M-Pesa reference {ref}. We check every paybill payment with M-Pesa before it is added to your balance — usually a few minutes. There is nothing more to do.
vendor.topup.phone: Phone to send the payment request to
vendor.topup.phoneHint: We will try to send an M-Pesa request to this number. If it does not arrive, you can still pay with the reference.
vendor.topup.referenceAlso: If the prompt does not arrive, quote this
vendor.topup.refused: The last request was not paid
vendor.push.title: Get told, without watching this page
vendor.push.reason: We will tell you when a payment you made is confirmed and when a buyer's order needs shipping — on this device, even when the tab is closed.
vendor.keys.title: Shipping API keys
vendor.secret.title: Signing secret
vendor.secret.body: Your secret signs every status update we send your shop system. It does not sign anybody in. Replace it regularly, whenever it may have been seen, and if you have lost it: all it takes is your password.
vendor.secret.bodyNoAccount: Your secret opens this console and signs every status update we send your shop system. Set up your email and password above, and the secret is only for your systems.
vendor.secret.warn: From the moment you rotate, status updates are signed with the new secret — give it to your shop system straight away. Every other device signed in to your store is signed out.
vendor.secret.newBody: This is the only time it is shown. Save it where your shop system and your team can find it, then close.
vendor.keys.note: What the shipping API sees when your site calls it. You do not need one to ask for prices — a key gives you your own rate limit, the cost breakdown, and the right to create shipments.
vendor.keys.kindPublishableNote: Safe to put in your product page and in the shipping button. It can ask for prices, and nothing else.
vendor.keys.kindSecretNote: Never put this in a page. It can create shipments and see what each stop charges. Shown once, then we keep only a fingerprint of it.
vendor.keys.modeTestNote: Every check runs, nothing is created and nothing is billed. Build against this one.
vendor.keys.label: What is it for? (optional)
vendor.keys.madePublishable: Copy this into your page. You can read it here again whenever you need it.
vendor.keys.madeSecret: Copy it now. This is the only time we can show it to you — we keep a fingerprint, not the key.
vendor.keys.madeWhere: Send it in the X-SBG-Key header, or as the key attribute on the shipping button.
vendor.keys.revokeBody: Anything still using it stops working straight away. Make the replacement first if you can — you can have as many keys as you like.
vendor.books.balanceSubEmpty: Your money in, out and net — for whatever you filter to below.
vendor.books.title: Bookkeeping
vendor.books.noEntriesLong: No entries yet. Top up or ship an order and it lands in your books.
